And to answer your questions:

  • No, they can not be potty trained. Chickens you can teach to go in a specific area and to even poo on command (I have never raised indoor chickens, but have had my share of pet ones. My friend has an indoor.). Ducks technically have no control, they just go when they go. The nice thing is, it's super watery and easy to clean up. They also will always go in water, it's like a trigger, lol. ---- You can buy or make duck diapers. My babies live outside and when they come inside I usually lay down a sheet then when I clean up just run the swiffer over the floors. We have stone floors, so it's easy.

  • They can be affectionate. Mine aren't as much as my goose was. But my goose was literally a part of me for her first 4 months while these ducks had each other so grew independent quite quickly. But they do like hugs and pets. Bird hugs they come up to you and rest their head on your shoulder, it's very sweet. They will also preen you, check you for parasites and stuff like that. Lots of nibbling involved.

  • Yes. Except they hate my cats and dogs so I have to keep them separated. They like the outside more. They are a foraging animal so like to dig, tear and make a mess of things. Being water fowl, they also love to swim and when they don't get to swim they can become ornery. But ducks are all different. I have seen others get along perfectly well with animals. My goose, for example, loved snuggling with dogs. The only reason my ducks are inside is because one became injured and I am nursing her to health. My drake is super protective of her and I don't want him left outside alone (also, this breed is a very docile breed. You should get at least 2 females for 1 male if you decide to get multiple ducks. Cayugas are an exception.)

  • Some ducks have bigger teeth than others. But technically yes they do, they're more like multiple little sharp nubs along the bill. They don't hurt that bad if they do bite you, though the twisting motion they do with their head is another story.....

  • Depends on the ducks. My duck doesn't get violent, she just gets scared. My drake, however, will puff up to try and make himself bigger and then buffet you with his chest. If he gets really mad, he will get a bill full of your skin and pinch it really damn hard. He bit me for the first time the other day cause I was moving his lady and he didn't approve, haha! They will also beat stuff with their wings, drop their heads and charge and hiss - but that's against things they really hate.

  • Heck naw. As mentioned above, ducks don't have control over their business and it's pretty watery. A duck diaper is only good for a few before you have to change it. There's no way. But I will say, I wish. Because omg the drake is the fluffiest, softest thing ever. I love picking him up and just cuddle squeezing him. And rubbing under his breast feathers.

  • Cayugas are ducks bred specifically for meat use. They are too heavy for their wings to lift, however there are a few that luck out (and I assume wild Cayugas have a better chance). Neither of mine can fly but they do like to lift 3 feet off the ground when I bring out their treats. Most people who get flying birds either clip their wings or pinion them. I am not a fan of the second (cutting the tendon of the wing so it can't use it to fly) and I feel bad clipping wings and stopping flying animals from flying. So I specifically look for non-flying breeds.

backyardchickens.com is a great website to learn more about raising birds of numerous kinds. I would suggest having a nice large yard if you get more than one. One duck you can make it a lot more personal, but they are social animals so I am aiming for a flock once we get a bigger house.
